label: Technique Murray 1: a 3 ft wind sea down the course

test.title: Murray 1: a 3 ft wind sea down the course
test.purpose: Practise the whole sequence in a plain 3 ft wind sea (4.2 s, 28 m waves) running down the course. Murray Stewart's cues (Rottnest camp, November 2026): catch a wave, as square as needed; stay high on its face (ease off, let the push hold you); scan 3 to 8 m ahead of the bow, within 30 degrees either side, for darker patches on the back faces ahead; when one is in reach, sprint to drop and move to it, to be on the upper part of the next wave's face there; prefer running diagonal to square.
lookFor: the darker patches on the back faces 3 to 8 m ahead (the near-face shading C2 is on: faceres=1)
where you sit on the face when you ease off, and how long the push holds you there
what the next wave does where you saw a dark patch
questions: Do the dark patches show where the next steep face comes up, there or half a wavelength on?
Does staying high and dropping on a dark patch give longer or more linked rides than paddling steadily?
Is 3 to 8 m the right place to look in this sea?
test.compare: faceres=0 in the address for the shading without C2; &guide=1&coaching=1 to see what the route finder would do.
